_comment: Narration for the Duum demo (out/duum/cut.mp4, 68.2s, 5 scenes). Each cue names the BEAT it lands on, from that scene's .beats.jsonl, so the voice tracks the picture. Budgeted at Brian's MEASURED 2.9 words/sec. REWRITTEN 2026-08-19 for the sound release: the film now carries the guest's own audio as a bed under the narration, so the score and the effects are audible rather than described. Claims checked against source this session: the effects mixer is 8 voices summed into the DMA ring in pc64/snd_pcm.c (it does NOT take the ring from the music - that is the whole design); the score is the WAD's own file handed to unomedia's MIDI player by pc64/snd_mus.c; Freedoom ships its music as finished Standard MIDI Files and the engine now passes those through unchanged; the Controls screen is filled by uno.bind_name, i.e. it reads pc64's binding table; render() and the game logic are Python and only the span writers are C. The WAD is Freedoom (BSD), never id's.
_voice: Brian - Deep, Resonant and Comforting (matches arin's UnoDOS OS demo and the previous Duum film)

cues.text: This is Doom, written entirely in Python, running as an app inside UnoDOS.
And now you can hear it: the game file's own score.
The world streams out of the WAD as you walk. This one is Freedoom, freely redistributable.
Every sound is the WAD's own.
Mixed over the music, not instead of it.
Escape brings up the pause menu.
The Controls screen asks the operating system what each action is bound to, so this list is the machine's own key table, not a picture of one.
The geometry and the game logic are Python. Only the per-pixel drawing is C.
Every other port of this system rebuilds its apps per machine. Duum does the reverse.
